item.title: Provider Admin Role
item.description:
Provider Administrator 🔗

What is the purpose of this role?

  • Used for administration of Layer5 Cloud.
  • Used for debugging and monitoring.
  • Applicable to platform engineering team and on-prem users.

Who can assign this role?

  • Provider Admins

When this role first assigned?

  • On ☁️ boot-up (using build args)

How many instances of these roles?

  • Any number, on every plan. Layer5 Cloud does not guard the last Provider Admin. A Provider Admin can remove the role from every Provider Admin, themselves included. Only a Provider Admin assigns or removes provider roles (Provider Admin, Kanvas, and Curator). Kanvas is granted automatically at sign-up and holds no keychains. Curator holds no keychains in a default install.

Who can remove assignment of this role?

item.title: Default Organization Roles
item.description:
Default Organization Roles

Organization Administrators 🔗

What is the purpose of this role?

  • Administration of an organization (for each organization for which the user has this role assigned)

Who can assign this role?

  • An Organization Admin of that organization, a holder of Assign User Roles there, or a Provider Admin. The person must already be a member, unless the caller is a Provider Admin.

When this role first assigned?

item.title: Default Workspace Roles
item.description:
Workspace Administrator 🔗

What is the purpose of this role?

  • Managing workspaces, environments, teams, and lifecycle actions, and reviewing catalog requests, in each organization where the user holds the role. It is not limited to a single workspace, and there is no Workspace Owner role that assigns it.

Who can assign this role?

item.title: Default Team Roles
item.description:
Default Team Roles

Team Administrator 🔗

What is the purpose of this role?

  • Administering one team. The keys apply across every organization the team is mapped into, not only inside the team. The role includes team, user-viewing, and security management permissions.

Who can assign this role?

  • Team Admin of that team, an Organization Admin or holder of Assign User Roles for a team mapped to the organization, or a Provider Admin. Teams accept no other role.

When this role first assigned?

item.title: Default User Role
item.description:
Default User Role

User 🔗

What is the purpose of this role?

  • To grant Organization members access to basic features and resources within the context of that Organization.

Who can assign this role?

  • An Organization Admin of that organization, a holder of Assign User Roles there, or a Provider Admin. Workspace Admin and Team Admin do not assign organization roles. Team scope accepts only Team Admin.

When this role first assigned?

item.title: Identity and Security
item.description:
Organizations are the basic unit of multi-tenancy inside of Layer5 Cloud. The identity structure is flexible: an organization has any number of teams, a team has any number of members, and a user can belong to any number of teams and organizations.

Identity and security answer two questions for every request: who is acting, and what that person may do in the organization the request runs in. Organization membership, the roles a person holds in that organization, and resources shared with them directly each contribute. The same person can hold different access in each organization they belong to.

item.title: Default Academy Roles
item.description:
Academy Administrator

Academy Administrator 🔗

What is the purpose of this role?

  • Management of an organization’s academy, learner management, and access to academy instructor console.

Who can assign this role?

  • Organization Administrators

When this role first assigned?

  • Manually assigned by an Organization Administrator.

How many instances of these roles?

  • Min: 0, Max: many

Who can remove assignment of this role?

item.title: Roles
item.description:
Roles map permissions to users. Roles contain any number of keychains, which contain any number of keys (permissions). Assign roles to users to grant permissions.

Provider Admin Role 🔗

Provider Admin Role

What is the purpose of this role?

  • Used for administration of Layer5 Cloud.
  • Used for debugging and monitoring.
  • Applicable to platform engineering team and on-prem users.

Who can assign this role?

item.title: Keychains
item.description:
In Layer5 Cloud, a collection of permissions is represented as a keychain. One or more keychains are grouped together and assigned to a role. Later, a role can be assigned to a user. This is the general flow of how keychains reach a user.

  • A key allows one action, such as Create Token.
  • A keychain groups related keys, such as everything needed to manage teams.
  • A role groups keychains, and users hold roles in an organization or team.

A user’s effective keys in an organization are the union of the keys in every keychain of every role the user holds there. A keychain grants nothing by itself. It takes effect only through a role that includes it.

item.title: Keys
item.description:
In Layer5 Cloud, permissions are represented as keys, each serving as a unique identifier for a specific permission. One or more keys can be grouped together and assigned to a keychain. Then this keychain can be assigned to a role and that role can be assigned to a user. A user never receives a key directly. This is the general flow of how keys reach a user.

Keys, keychains, and roles are defined once for the whole Layer5 Cloud deployment. They are not copied or customized per organization. What varies per organization is which roles a user holds there. A user’s effective keys in an organization are the union of the keys from every role they hold in that organization, so the same person can hold a key in one organization and lack it in another. Holding an additional role only adds keys. It never removes any. Provider Admin holds every key and passes every check in every organization. For how this fits with authentication and cross-organization resource sharing, see Security Boundaries.

item.title: Sessions
item.description:
What sessions are 🔗

A session is the credential Layer5 Cloud issues each time someone signs in. It is what keeps a browser tab, a second device, or a connected Meshery Server signed in, and it is what you end when you want one of those sign-ins to stop working. Sessions expire on their own. API tokens do not.

Layer5 Cloud sessions use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. OAuth 2.0 is a standard protocol for authorization and focuses on client developer simplicity while providing specific authorization flows for web applications, desktop applications, mobile phones, and so on.
